summary:
Radar for 26 Nov 2026 (Thanksgiving). There are two fresh, verified hooks and both are in the GLP-1 niche.
(1) Health Canada warned on 25 Nov about NAION, a very rare vision-loss condition, with semaglutide. It reviewed 23 cases and says it is assessing all GLP-1s. This comes on top of the FDA's class-wide label change. It is in mainstream news everywhere (CBC, CTV, Globe, Toronto Star, Bloomberg), so the topic is peaking. Our differentiated angle is a label-based explainer that names tirzepatide and lists which symptoms need urgent care. It should also refresh the held Serious Risks video.
(2) An RSNA 2026 study (Brigham, 107 women, retrospective, released 24 Nov) found breast density rose in 62.5% of GLP-1 users and 22.4% were called back after a screening mammogram. TODAY, NY Post, Fox, Medical News Today and Everyday Health covered it, but creator coverage is still thin. It's a calm 'Is this normal?' moment with real search intent and a reassuring explanation: fat loss makes the dense tissue look more prominent. The evidence is weak, so word it as 'linked to' and send people to talk to their imaging team.
Holiday: the Thanksgiving morning-after Shorts peak today and tomorrow.
Pipeline: Foundayo's ATTAIN-OSA results (AHI −43.8% without PAP; FDA filing planned by end of 2026) and retatrutide's TRIUMPH-OSA results (up to −60.6%) are a sleep apnea story. It is best told through Zepbound, which is already approved for obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity.
Evergreen search formats still carry the channel: hair loss, nausea (refreshed by HCPLive's '53% get GI symptoms within 5 years' coverage), after 6 months, stopping and keeping results (Medscape hook), pen and vial IFU how-tos, injection-site 'Is this normal?' and a Mounjaro vs Ozempic nausea Short that feeds the live SURPASS-2 video.
Smaller emerging hooks: sleep and weight loss on GLP-1 (observational) and 'Nature's Ozempic' oats (Guardian), both under the natural-support pillar, plus checking your other medicines as weight drops (Medscape).
Rejected: the Greenwich Rx compounded recall and counterfeit-site stories, retatrutide decoy busts and gray-market peptide stories, the online tirzepatide price index, Medicare and coverage news, the Tencent animal-stage 'AI drug beats Wegovy' story, the colonic pseudo-obstruction case report, semaglutide in children aged 6–11 and the observational cancer studies.
Don't re-script anything already made or live (Foundayo What to Expect, Mounjaro vs Ozempic SURPASS-2, Months 2–6, MASH, After 6 Months). Re-render those instead.

candidates.topic: GLP-1 weight loss and mammograms: a new RSNA 2026 study (107 women) found breast density rose in 62.5% and 22.4% were called back for more imaging. Is this normal, and what should you tell your imaging team?
candidates.angle: Calm 'Is this normal?' explainer. Getting called back after a mammogram on Mounjaro or Ozempic is common in this small study. The likely reason is that fat loss makes the dense tissue look more prominent; there is no evidence the drugs cause cancer. The practical step is to tell the breast imaging team you're on a GLP-1 and how much weight you've lost. Make clear it is a small retrospective conference study ('linked to', not 'causes'), keep screening as recommended, and add the talk-to-your-doctor line.
candidates.why_now: Released at RSNA on 24 Nov. In 48 hours it reached TODAY (twice), NY Post, Fox News, Medical News Today, Everyday Health, Medical Daily and News-Medical: the mainstream stage has started, but there's almost no creator coverage yet. It affects a large share of our audience (women aged 40–65 due for screening), and the reassuring framing fits our tone. Plenty of women get a scary callback letter and then search for answers.

evidence.signal: Brigham and Women's study: 107 women on a GLP-1 ≥1 year, density increased in 62.5%, recall rate 22.4% (more than double average); greater weight loss linked to larger density increase
Conference coverage. The authors suggest fat loss makes fibroglandular tissue look more prominent
Mainstream pickup on 24 Nov: 'GLP-1s tied to higher breast density, mammogram recalls'
Science press pickup on 24 Nov

candidates.topic: Mounjaro, Zepbound and Ozempic vision warning (NAION): Health Canada's 25 Nov semaglutide warning after the FDA's class label change. What the label says, how rare it is, and which symptoms mean get help now
candidates.angle: Calm, label-first explainer that leads with tirzepatide. Health Canada reviewed 23 cases, calls the risk 'very rare' and is assessing all GLP-1s. Then the US label wording, then the symptoms that need urgent care: sudden, painless vision loss or blurring in one eye. Close with questions to bring to your prescriber. Don't make a standalone fear video. Use it as the fresh hook to finally ship the held Serious Risks video (re-timed, NAION chapter refreshed) and for one calm Short. Never end a chapter on the warning card.
candidates.why_now: Health Canada warned on 25 Nov. Since then CBC, CTV, the Globe and Mail, the Toronto Star, CP24 and Bloomberg ('Patients claim GLP-1s caused vision loss') have covered it, along with Fox 5 on the FDA warning and an Ophthalmology Times Q&A. Search demand is spiking in Canada and the US right now. Our NAION post was a TikTok top performer (630).

evidence.signal: Health Canada warns of a 'very rare but serious' NAION risk with semaglutide (Ozempic, Rybelsus, Wegovy)
23 cases reviewed (12 Canadian). Health Canada is assessing all GLP-1s and says to get urgent care for blurring or sudden vision loss
The US FDA adds the GLP-1 NAION warning that the Canadian Wegovy monograph already carried (Sept 2026)

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving on tirzepatide, the morning after: still full, stomach pain, bloating and heartburn after the big plate. Is this normal?
candidates.angle: Felt-symptom Shorts for the 20:00 holiday slot today and tomorrow. Lead with the drug, put the relief fact in the same sentence (slower gastric emptying is how the medicine works), give a short when-to-call-your-doctor line, and link to the Thanksgiving long video. Skip diet tips that don't have a felt moment.
candidates.why_now: It's Thanksgiving Day. ABC, NPR, KFOR, FOX 7, 11Alive, WAND and ConsumerAffairs all ran GLP-1 Thanksgiving pieces on 25 Nov. Our own winners: full the morning after 495, stuffing 329, stomach pain 274.

evidence.signal: 'As GLP-1 use grows, patients and doctors rethink Thanksgiving dinner' (25 Nov)
'Nutritionist shares how those on a GLP-1 can navigate Thanksgiving' (25 Nov)

candidates.topic: Foundayo (orforglipron) pill: nausea and food questions people are searching, now that it's in Australian, Canadian and UK pharmacies
candidates.angle: Never re-script the Foundayo What to Expect video (ssb7Zcs3KSY). Instead, feed it with Shorts that pair Foundayo with a practical question people search: 'Foundayo nausea: is it normal on a pill?' and 'Do you have to take Foundayo on an empty stomach?' Use label wording only and no dose amounts. Each Short links to ssb7Zcs3KSY. The ATTAIN-OSA sleep apnea result (AHI −43.8% without PAP at 52 weeks; FDA filing planned) can be one supporting fact, never the topic.
candidates.why_now: It has been in our snapshots 6 times at momentum 88–90. Foundayo is newly launched in AU, CA and UK, and fresh ATTAIN-OSA results (AHA 2026) keep it in the news. Lilly's Medicare Part D Foundayo page (23 Nov) adds US search. Our Foundayo nausea Short had 845 views and the Thanksgiving one 900.

Lilly plans to file Foundayo with the FDA for OSA after the phase 3 win
'Orforglipron reduces sleep apnea severity in ATTAIN-OSA' (24 Nov)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: why it's more common in women (label 5.4% vs 0.9% on placebo; women 7.1% vs 1.3%), when shedding shows up, and whether it grows back
candidates.angle: Felt-symptom search format. The 'Is this normal?' relief comes in sentence one: the label rate, the link to rapid weight loss, and what usually happens next. A dermatology survey from J Cosmet Dermatol (Aug 2026) can be one supporting line. Use for a Short and for retitling the existing Hair Loss video ('Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Hair Loss: Why More in Women?'). Don't make a new long video.
keywords: does hair grow back after mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Flat at 79–80 across 6 snapshots, so demand is steady. Our hair Short is the channel's top 'Is this normal?' Short (1,035). The existing long video's 0.79% CTR needs the title fix.

evidence.signal: US cross-sectional survey of dermatological and hair consequences of GLP-1-mediated weight loss

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide nausea: why it happens, when it usually eases, and what may help (refreshed by HCPLive's '53% of GLP-1 users get GI symptoms within 5 years' and a new semaglutide dose-formulation GI network meta-analysis)
candidates.angle: Lead with the drug and the felt symptom. Sentence one: label nausea is mostly during dose escalation and decreases over time. The new data is one supporting line: GI symptoms are common, and the meta-analysis found higher dose meant more GI events (semaglutide, so name the drug correctly). Then 2–3 practical tips: smaller meals, eat slower, stop at full. Say when to call a clinician. No dose advice.
candidates.why_now: HCPLive (25 Nov) and Pharmacy Times (25 Nov, 'GLP-1 RA adverse effects: what pharmacists should monitor') put GI side effects back in the news. There's also a fresh network meta-analysis in Front Endocrinol (10 Nov). It has sat at 79–80 in 5 snapshots.

evidence.signal: 'GI symptoms affect an estimated 53% of GLP-1 RA users within 5 years' (25 Nov)
Dose-response network meta-analysis of GI adverse events with subcutaneous and oral semaglutide in type 2 diabetes

candidates.topic: Mounjaro vs Ozempic: which caused more nausea and stomach side effects in SURPASS-2? (approved-drug head-to-head)
candidates.angle: Short-only head-to-head that feeds the live SURPASS-2 long video (s9wRqHkfu0o). Don't make a new long video. Sentence one: 'Mounjaro vs Ozempic: which upset more stomachs?' Give GI rates per arm as reported, with the population on screen: adults with type 2 diabetes on metformin, 40 weeks, vs semaglutide 1 mg. The relief fact: it mostly eases after dose escalation. No dose advice. Ride the 'Ozempic' search spike from the Health Canada news.
keywords: which is easier on the stomach mounjaro or ozempic
candidates.why_now: Head-to-heads against tirzepatide are a proven 10x search format in this niche. The SURPASS-2 long video is live but still missing its brand-name title. The Ozempic news spike (NAION) is lifting 'Ozempic' search right now.

evidence.signal: Fresh GI dose-response evidence for semaglutide (supporting context)
'GLP-1 RA adverse effects: what pharmacists should monitor' (25 Nov)

candidates.angle: Feeds the Stopping → Keeping Results series, our fastest grower. Put the result and the population in one sentence, then the habits with evidence (protein, strength training, follow-up with your prescriber). Never advise stopping or switching. Use it for Shorts that link to Stopping, and for retitle or end-screen work. The Keeping Results long video already exists, so don't remake it.

how to keep weight off after ozempic

candidates.topic: Zepbound sleep apnea: how tirzepatide's approved OSA use compares with this month's new pill and triple-agonist trials (ATTAIN-OSA, TRIUMPH-OSA)
candidates.angle: Answer 'Forget Zepbound?' headlines with the approved drug first. Zepbound is already approved for moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. Then put the two November phase 3 results in context as not yet approved: orforglipron AHI −43.8% without PAP; retatrutide up to −60.6% in TRIUMPH-1-OSA. These are separate trials, not a head-to-head, and we say so. This is a fast-turn candidate that rides 'retatrutide' search without making a 'What is X?' video. Never mention where to get retatrutide.
candidates.why_now: Both readouts appeared at AHA in November. On 24 Nov, Motley Fool and Yahoo ran 'Forget Zepbound: retatrutide cut sleep apnea severity by up to 60%', plus 2 Minute Medicine and the BHF on retatrutide. Retatrutide search is high (it's also in gray-market news). We already have a Sleep Apnea long video, so this must be a new angle, or a chapter or Short, not a repeat.

evidence.signal: TRIUMPH-OSA: retatrutide reduces sleep apnea severity in OSA plus obesity
ATTAIN-OSA: oral GLP-1 linked to fewer breathing interruptions
'Forget Zepbound: Lilly's retatrutide just cut sleep apnea severity by up to 60%' (24 Nov)

candidates.topic: Losing weight on tirzepatide? Why your other medicines (blood pressure, diabetes) may need a check-in with your doctor (Medscape, 25 Nov)
candidates.angle: Broad Lane A topic that sits naturally next to big Mounjaro videos. Feeling dizzy or shaky as the weight comes off can be a reason to talk to your prescriber. The label notes low blood sugar 'may be higher' with insulin or a sulfonylurea, and it is also reported without type 2 diabetes. Never tell anyone to change or stop a medicine; the whole message is 'bring this list to your doctor'. Works as a 'questions for your doctor' chapter or a Short ('Dizzy on Mounjaro?').

candidates.topic: 'Nature's Ozempic': can oats and fibre really boost your own GLP-1? (Guardian, 25 Nov)
candidates.angle: Myth-correction plus natural-support pillar, in a positive tone. Fibre such as oat beta-glucan can support fullness and blood sugar and may nudge your own GLP-1 release. It's nowhere near the medicine, and that's fine: it helps alongside it. Don't cite the mouse study as a human result.
candidates.why_now: The Guardian (25 Nov) reports oat sales soaring. FoodNavigator ran '5 emerging GLP-1 trends' and Grocery Dive covered household spending. Consumer interest is mainstream and evidence-led creators are scarce.

evidence.signal: 'Nature's Ozempic': oat sales soar as shoppers seek out foods that mimic GLP-1s (25 Nov)

evidence.source: PubMed / Eur J Nutr (mouse study, context only)
evidence.signal: Oat protein hydrolysate and beta-glucan improved glycemic control in obese mice. Not a human result

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines for weight in women with PCOS: a new meta-analysis of randomized trials
candidates.angle: Who-may-benefit pillar for women aged 25–45. The RCT meta-analysis supports weight loss in PCOS with overweight or obesity. PCOS itself isn't an approved use, so frame it as 'questions to bring to your doctor'. Best as a chapter or Short, not its own long video yet.
candidates.why_now: A systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs was published in Minerva Endocrinol on 18 Nov. There's no mainstream coverage yet, and 'ozempic pcos' has steady search demand.

evidence.signal: Meta-analysis of RCTs: GLP-1 RA weight-loss effects in reproductive-age women with PCOS
